goals.title: Hot glass, your own breath
goals.critique: The verb is concrete and new for a game: you blow, turn and tip a cooling glob against the clock, and a body really does the work, so it sits right on the human's line of real physics and Lumi's hands holding and turning things. The road is long and risky, though. Live thin-shell glass that inflates, sags and bursts at its thinnest point is a research project, and it is already 35 ms a step on the CPU. What comes after the bubble (creatures drinking from a crooked rim, a shelf of history) is charming but low-stakes, and the loop is one craft at one furnace, not a world of material. Burst clips can go around once; whether players come back depends on the blowing feeling like a skill and not like a slider minigame, and the pitch only claims that, it doesn't show it.

goals.title: Burn a hole with a lens you blew
goals.critique: This is the best showcase for a path tracer, and the leaf catching under a crooked dot is a real picture. As play it is thin: tilting a lens until a dot shrinks is a one-minute trick, and rainbows and telescopes are a list of optics demos with no loop or stakes joining them. The pitch mixes blowing, grinding, prisms, mirrors and telescopes, so it never says what the player does all evening. Grinding a lens and the light obeying your curve is the strong core, but the road treats it as one step among many.

goals.title: The island has a voice in every thing
goals.critique: Knock anything, chip it until it is in tune, and have the creatures play your song back with your mistakes left in: that is a clear chain, and five creatures playing a slightly sour song is something people would really send to a friend. Physical modes are not a mechanic on their own, though. Tuning by chipping can become a tedious pitch-meter puzzle, and once the band exists there is little reason to keep playing. It touches 'everything is material you work', but sound is the only property that counts. The road is sensible and already half there with modes.jl, which is a strength and also a sign of how safe it is.

goals.title: Dig the sea in
goals.critique: It is the most immediately readable: dig, wall off, the tide comes, everything washes away. Every minute has a verb and a clock, and the breach carrying Truffle off on bark is a moment people would clip. The weakness is that it is a beach-sandcastle sandbox people have seen in many fluid toys, so it will not be remembered as new. It also stands or falls on whether Maelstrom can run live in a box the size of a beach, which the road assumes rather than proves. It is built squarely on the human's direction (dig material, physics that breaks by what it is, water that carries things), but it needs something of its own beyond 'real water and sand' to be named after.
